page: Google Cloud Platform m4n-ultramem-224 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the m4n server family. It features 224 dedicated virtual CPUs (vCPUs) and 5952.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of approximately 26.57 GB per core. This configuration is designed specifically for memory-intensive enterprise workloads.

This server type does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPU hardware, meaning all storage requirements must be met via network-attached storage options. Additionally, it does not include any complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The lack of local NVMe storage and GPU acceleration represents a clear tradeoff, positioning this instance strictly for memory-bound CPU tasks rather than local-storage-heavy IOPS or hardware-accelerated graphics and machine learning workloads.

From a cost efficiency perspective, the m4n-ultramem-224 represents a high-density resource profile where the primary investment is directed toward massive RAM capacity and dedicated compute resources. It is engineered for workloads such as large-scale in-memory databases, enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems, and massive data warehousing operations that require keeping exceptionally large datasets entirely in system memory to avoid disk latency.
